sections.content: The plan preserves lifecycle ownership and requires hash-bound, fail-closed evidence across coordinator recovery, authorization freshness, legacy handling, dogfood, and completion handoff. Published or LKG replay may tolerate same-selection catalog drift, while authority, selection, resource, and semantic drift block progress.
sections.title: Recovery requirements

sections.content: The migration bridge materializes fixed RED tests only for R0 through R2 and writes declared test files only. The plan-local validator maps R0 through R4 to source tests, derives canonical validator and candidate identities, validates slice selection, and emits snapshot fields.
sections.title: Migration and validation

sections.content: The terminal validator executes registered repo-bound commands, validates contracts, manifests, receipts, authority, knowledge, freeze, and skill-input bindings, then publishes a non-authorizing implementation receipt on full success. Candidate source manifests exclude generated evidence and bind source content identity; integrity tests verify stable roots and source-change detection.
sections.title: Terminal completion
